doc.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011

title: Mentors, especially Jack Palmer
summary: Rowe asks about older mentors. Montalbano names Jack Palmer, the Mancusos, Chick Esposito, Sal Amico, J.R. Monterose, Sal Nistico and Nick Brignola, and says Palmer taught him business and conduct.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: That’s neat. Well you mentioned a thing about playing with older musicians, and I know that there’s been some good mentors in this area, even though I didn’t grow up here when I got here I started to recognize people that were from that older generation.
Who were those people for you?

Well early on Jack Palmer, a huge mentor for me. And of course Sammy Mancuso and Dolores Mancuso. Chick Esposito. You know when we were involved in that band and I would hang out with Chick a lot and do gigs with him and I learned a lot of stuff from him, and then later with Sal Amico, I mean later, like in my later teen years. Sal Amico and then of course J.R. [Monterose] and Sal Nistico and Nick Brignola. But initially I would say Jack Palmer, a huge influence. Not only about the music but about business, how to conduct yourself on a gig, how to talk to people.

Yes. Oh he would tell you too. Yeah, he’d take you aside if you did something that wasn’t quite up to his standards you know. Yeah, he would tell you. And he had, as you know, you knew Jack and I saw some of that interview you did with him, which was fantastic. He was quite a guy.
